paragraphs.text: Bots for DeepSeek Harness: persistent AI individuals with their own conversation, workspace and memo
ry, who work with you and with each other.
# dsh-futurebot
Bots for DeepSeek Harness.
A bot is a persistent AI individual. It has a name, standing instructions from you, its own workspac
e, and its own conversation, which continues across days and tasks. It keeps a memory that only it w
rites, pursues an agenda it can revise, hands work to other bots and picks up their answers, and wor
ks in groups toward goals.
This plugin is a working design prototype of the Bot discussed in the Perspective *The second half o
f harness design: from agents to Bots*. It is a usable prototype of the design and does not represen
t the implementation discussed in the paper. The Perspective proposes five conditions for a mature B
ot. The first four can be checked operationally, and this repository includes scripts that test each
of them against a live Harness.
| Condition in the Perspective | What the plugin provides | Test |
| Continuing earlier work | One ongoing conversation per bot; work between bots survives restarts |

`c1-continuing.mjs` |
| Learning from experience | Memory written only by the bot: records, conclusi

ons and corrections, kept apart | `c2-learning.mjs` |
| Revising its plans | An agenda whose every c

hange carries a reason; folders it watches wake it with new evidence | `c3-revising.mjs` |
| Long-te
rm collaboration | Notes on each collaborator; delegation between bots; groups with staged goals | `
c4-collaboration.mjs` |
The fifth condition, consciousness, is outside what software features can establish. The plugin make
s no claim about it.
**Status: 0.1.0-alpha.** Works against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1`. Interfaces and stored data may
change before 0.1.0.
## Requirements
- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` or a later `0.2.x` release. Prereleases are published under npm's `n

ext` tag, not `latest`.
- Node.js 24.9 or later and pnpm on your `PATH` (the Harness uses pnpm to in

stall plugins).
- A model the Harness can use. The examples assume DeepSeek with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`

l plugins).
- A model the Harness can use. The examples assume DeepSeek with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` set.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`dsh plugin add` links this directory into the `web` profile. Open the address `dsh web` prints. A *
*Bots** entry appears in the sidebar.
## First steps
1. Open **Bots** and choose **New bot**. Give it a name and instructions, for example *Lin, analyses

transcriptomics data*. Its workspace defaults to `~/futurebots/<name>`.
2. Create a second bot and

tick **Coordinator**. The coordinator receives your requests and hands work to the others.
3. Choose
**Open conversation** on the coordinator and ask it for something that needs the analyst, for examp
le *Ask Lin how many primes there are below 10,000 and tell me.* The coordinator sends the work; Lin
answers in its own conversation; the answer comes back by itself and the coordinator reports to you

.
4. Open **Details** on a bot to see its memory, agenda, watched folders and its work with other bo

ts.
5. Under **Groups**, create a group with an admin and ask it for a goal in stages. The admin pla
ns; you press **Start**; each stage goes to its owner and the admin checks it.
## What a bot can do
Each bot's conversation gets these tools. Ordinary Harness conversations do not.
| Tool | Purpose |
| `bot_list`, `bot_send` | See the other bots; give one a message or a piece of work. The recipient'
s final answer in the turn that handled the work comes back to the sender automatically and wakes it

. |
| `memory_note`, `memory_search` | Keep and look up records, conclusions and corrections. A corr
ection marks what it replaces instead of deleting it. A note can be about the user or another bot. |
| `agenda_update` | Add, revise, reorder, finish or drop goals, always with a reason and, when ther

e is one, the evidence that prompted it. |
| `watch_folder` | Be woken when files in a folder change

while the bot is idle. Changes the bot makes itself do not count. |
| `search_own` | Search the bot

's own conversation, including turns that no longer fit in context. |
| `goal_plan`, `goal_check` |
For a group's admin: plan a goal in stages and check each finished stage. |
Bots can also use whatever tools the Harness gives their base agent, including the Harness's own sch
eduling tool for waking at a given time.
## Permissions and approvals
Each bot has one of three permissions, mapped onto the Harness's own controls:
- **Read only**: read-only sandbox. Writing or running anything that changes files needs your approv

al each time.
- **Work in its workspace**: writes and runs commands inside its workspace. Anything o

utside needs your approval.
- **Allow everything**: no sandbox and no approvals.
Before the Harness asks you, the plugin answers some approval requests itself:
- If a bot is set to ask once per conversation (the default for new bots) and you already allowed th

e same kind of operation in that conversation, the request is allowed.
- In a group whose admin revi
ews first, the admin judges a member's request with one short model call. It can deny the request, a
nd the member is told why. It can pass the request to you. It can approve only if you turned that on

for the group. Each decision is recorded in the group log.
- Everything else, including any review
that fails or takes too long, goes to you.
## How it maps onto the Harness
The plugin never runs its own agent loop and never writes custom session events.
| Bot property | Harness mechanism |
| Conversation and workspace | An ordinary session in a Workspace registered for the bot's folder |
| Identity, team, memory, agenda, group rules | Prompt contexts registered on that session's agent.
The system prompt and tool list stay identical across bots, so they share a prompt-cache prefix. Mem
ory and agenda refresh at most every ten turns, because the Harness logs a full snapshot each time c

ontext text changes. |
| Work between bots and group messages | Follow-up turns with the plugin's ow
n message source; `session/event` (`user/message`, `assistant/message`, `turn/end`) tells which turn

handled which piece of work |
| Evidence | A file-system watch per watched folder |
| Approvals | A

n `approval/request` listener placed ahead of the user's prompt |
